classification.difficultyReason: Translate the absence of horizontal tangents into a derivative condition, factor the parameterised derivative, and justify positivity for every real x using n>0.

content.prompt: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Show that the function $$f(x)=x(x^2+1)^n$$ will never be horizontal at any point on the curve.

answer.short: $f'(x)=(x^2+1)^{n-1}[1+(2n+1)x^2]>0$ for every real $x$, so the curve has no horizontal tangent.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=(x^2+1)^n+x\cdot n(x^2+1)^{n-1}(2x)\\f'(x)&=(x^2+1)^{n-1}[1+(2n+1)x^2]>0.\end{align*}$$

 Since $n$ is a positive integer, both factors are positive for every real $x$. Thus $f'(x)$ is never zero.
